name: How do I add an authenticator account?
content: Open Menu 2FA from the menu bar, choose Settings, then tap +. Enter a title and your Base32 TOTP secret, or paste an otpauth:// URI. You can optionally choose an icon. Secrets stay on your Mac and are used only to generate codes locally.

name: How do I copy a code?
content: Left-click the Menu 2FA key in the menu bar and choose an account. The current 6-digit TOTP code is copied to the clipboard. While that menu is open, the key icon becomes a countdown ring for the 30-second period.

name: Where are my secrets stored?
content: Authenticator accounts and secrets remain locally on your Mac. Menu 2FA generates codes on-device and does not upload secrets or codes to the developer. Do not send secrets or recovery codes when contacting support.

name: Does Menu 2FA collect usage data?
content: No developer-operated analytics, behavioral tracking, or advertising systems are used. Your Menu 2FA configuration remains locally on your Mac.

name: Can Menu 2FA start automatically when I log in?
content: Yes. Enable Launch at Login from the Menu 2FA context menu (right-click the key). You can disable it again at any time there or in macOS Login Items.

name: I removed an account. Can I restore it?
content: Removed accounts cannot be recovered from Menu 2FA. Add the account again with the original secret if you still have it from the service that issued it.

name: Which platform is Menu 2FA designed for?
content: Menu 2FA is designed for macOS and is intended for distribution through the Mac App Store.
